rfm_tuples.R: Total non-performing assets as a percentage of total assets declined to 0.47% at December 31, 2024, compared with 0.69% at December 31, 2023.
rfm_tuples.f: Cross-check the headline NPA decline against the underlying portfolio components — specifically nonaccrual portfolio loans vs. serviced GNMA-guaranteed nonaccruals. The 10-K's own reconciliation table (and Q1 2025 10-Q) shows nonaccrual portfolio loans rose from $61.0M (YE23) to $90.2M (YE24) (+48%), while serviced GNMA-guaranteed nonaccruals fell from $90.2M to $12.0M. NPL ex-GNMA as % of assets actually rose from 0.33% to 0.42% — the underlying credit quality DETERIORATED.
rfm_tuples.M_value: Headline NPA decline (0.69%->0.47%) is mechanically driven by ~$78M reduction in GNMA-guaranteed nonaccruals (which carry no credit risk to the bank). Excluding GNMA, NPAs as % of assets WORSENED from 0.33% to 0.42%. Q1 2025 10-Q shows nonaccrual loans roughly flat at $99.7M vs $102.2M at YE24.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Mode B catch — management leads MD&A highlights with the favorable headline NPA ratio but the improvement is almost entirely composition shift (GNMA removals, not credit improvement). Underlying portfolio NPA ratio rose 9bps. This is honest disclosure (numbers are in the reconciliation table) but the framing is selective.

rfm_tuples.R: As of December 31, 2024, our C&D concentration as a percentage of capital totaled 63.3% and our CRE concentration, net of owner-occupied loans, as a percentage of capital totaled 267.9%.

Both below the company's internal 100%/300% limits and well below regulatory 300% trigger. Past-due CRE only 18 bps. Non-owner occupied CRE Office exposure is $1.247B (~5.9% of loans), of which $515M is Atlanta — concentrated but stress-tested.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Disclosure matches reality. CRE concentration is high in absolute terms but trending down. Office exposure ($1.25B) is the obvious soft spot but is geographically distributed and is being actively de-risked.

EDGAR FTS shows no third-party filings referencing Ameris in distress contexts.

rfm_tuples.R: The allowance for credit losses on loans at March 31, 2025 was $345.6 million, or 1.67% of total loans, compared with $338.1 million, or 1.63% of total loans, at December 31, 2024.
rfm_tuples.f: Compare ACL coverage trajectory and provision adequacy vs. underlying credit migration. Verify with FDIC call-report data (NALNLS, LNATRES, LNLSGR fields).
rfm_tuples.M_value: FDIC call-report pre-cutoff series (2024Q1 -> 2025Q1): NALNLS $165M->$179M->$96M->$102M->$100M; LNATRES $320M->$336M->$334M->$338M->$346M; coverage ratio (LNATRES/LNLSGR) ~1.53% -> 1.56% -> 1.55% -> 1.59% -> 1.63%. ACL coverage IS increasing and is now at a reasonable level for the portfolio mix. However Q1 2025 provision was $21.9M, lower than the level that would offset a downturn given $9.0M of NCOs.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: FDIC data confirms 10-K/10-Q disclosures. ACL coverage trajectory is appropriate — building reserves modestly faster than NCOs. No evidence of under-reserving.

rfm_tuples.R: Commercial and industrial substandard loans totaled $27.0 million at December 31, 2024 (vs $20.1M at YE23); C&I nonaccruals $11.9M (vs $8.1M at YE23); allowance allocated to C&I $87.2M (vs $64.1M at YE23, +36% YoY).
rfm_tuples.f: Mode B — derive whether the C&I credit deterioration is being acknowledged or obscured. Compute YoY changes in substandard, nonaccruals, charge-offs, and ACL allocation by portfolio. Compare to management narrative.

rfm_tuples.M_value: C&I substandard up 35% YoY; C&I nonaccruals up 47% YoY; current-period gross C&I charge-offs $53.9M (very high); ACL on C&I up 36% YoY (management is reserving more, but C&I is now 14% of loans with 25% of allowance). C&D substandard up from $2.3M to $4.1M (+78%) and C&D nonaccruals up from $0.3M to $3.7M (+13x). Management acknowledges 'updated economic forecast' as driver in MD&A but does not frame the C&I/C&D deterioration prominently.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Underlying C&I and C&D credit metrics are deteriorating materially while management narrative emphasizes the favorable headline NPA ratio. Reserves are being built (good), but framing in MD&A is selective. Not fraud — the numbers are all disclosed — but a forensic reader sees deterioration the MD&A summary glosses.

rfm_tuples.R: As of December 31, 2024, approximately 46.8% of our deposits were uninsured, and we rely on these deposits for liquidity.
rfm_tuples.f: Mode B — for a regional bank with high uninsured-deposit ratio post-SVB, verify (a) the metric is honestly disclosed, (b) uninsured-deposit trajectory, (c) liquidity coverage. Cross-check Q1 2025.
rfm_tuples.M_value: YE24: $10.24B uninsured of $21.72B total (46.8%). Q1 2025: $10.01B uninsured of $21.91B total (45.7%) — modestly improving. Of Q1 2025 uninsured, $3.07B (30.7%) is municipal deposits COLLATERALIZED with securities/letters of credit, leaving ~$6.94B truly at-risk (31.7% of deposits). FHLB availability $3.52B + FRB Discount Window $2.29B = $5.81B of available secondary liquidity. CET1 ratio rose to 12.87% in Q1 2025 from 12.65%.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Honest disclosure with full context. ~46% uninsured-deposit ratio is HIGH for a regional bank (peer median ~35%) but a third is collateralized municipal money, and liquidity buffers ($5.8B) cover roughly 84% of the at-risk uninsured base. Capital ratios are strengthening.

rfm_tuples.R: Securities portfolio unrealized losses: AFS $39.0M (non-credit), HTM $20.7M as of December 31, 2024.
rfm_tuples.f: Verify securities-portfolio mark-to-market loss exposure relative to capital. For regional banks post-SVB this is a key tail risk.
rfm_tuples.M_value: Combined unrealized loss exposure ~$60M against $3.75B shareholders' equity (1.6%) and $2.73B Tier 1 capital. HTM is small at $164.7M amortized cost. AFS portfolio is heavily UST/agency/MBS. No need to realize losses for liquidity per management; FHLB+FRB capacity = $5.8B.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Securities AOCI exposure is small and well-managed. This is NOT a SVB-style duration trap. Ameris ran an unremarkable AFS-heavy portfolio.

Edwards sold 7,500 sh @ $47.35 on 2024-03-07 ($355K). Total $914K — trivial for a $4B+ market-cap company over 16 months. 1 open-market buy in same window. No CEO/CFO open-market selling. summary: ABCB is a clean honest regional bank disclosure with mostly PASS R/f/M tuples. Two MODERATE flags: (1) headline NPA improvement is composition-driven by GNMA removals — underlying portfolio NPL ratio actually rose from 0.33% to 0.42%; (2) C&I and C&D substandard/nonaccrual loans deteriorated materially YoY (+35% to +13x) while MD&A framing emphasizes the favorable headline. Neither is fraud — full reconciliations are in the filing — but both are selective framing that an honest reader sees through. All other forensic signals are clean: KPMG Big 4 auditor since 2021 (upgrade from Crowe), no going-concern language, capital ratios strengthening (CET1 12.65%->12.87% in Q1 2025), insider trading muted ($914K of sales in 16 months pre-cutoff with no CEO/CFO selling), no counterparty mirror disclosures, CRE concentration trending down and below 300% regulatory trigger, securities AOCI exposure tiny (~$60M vs $3.75B equity), and the DOJ Jacksonville consent order is fully disclosed with no follow-on actions. -12% drawdown into cutoff appears to be sector-correlated weakness (KBW Regional Banking Index pressure) rather than ABCB-specific distress.
